notes: dc CALL 2026-07-22: Q2 2026 earnings call (webcast 1:30 PM PT), speakers Pichai, Schindler, Ashkenazi; transcript from Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_CALL_TRANSCRIPT (one call, saved verbatim in gather/raw_documents/av_transcript_GOOGL_2026Q2.json). The transcript has transcription errors against the release: it says other income and expense 'was $9.8 billion' (release: $98.0 billion) and API tokens 'per month' (release: 'per minute'). The release figures are used.

dc FRESHNESS: the latest results in the documents are Q2 2026 (release 2026-07-22, 10-Q 2026-07-23). No Q3 2026 release exists in the prefetch (identity filings list ends at the 2026-07-22 8-K). A third-party calendar (unverified, no company confirmation found) puts the Q3 2026 report on 2026-10-28 after the close; anything dated after 2026-10-27 is out of scope and the Q3 numbers are not citable at this as_of. If Q3 is released, results of that date are not citable until 2 days after it; rerun with as_of two days after.

dc MGMT 2026-07-22 (Ashkenazi): full-year 2026 CapEx guidance raised to $195-205bn from $180-190bn, 'primarily due to an acceleration in the delivery of capacity to meet growing demand'; CapEx to 'increase significantly in 2027', details at a later date. The prior $180-190bn is stated only as 'previous estimate' in the Q2 call; its issue date (Q1 call, presumably 2026-04-29) is not in the saved documents (the Q1 release carries no capex range), so only the 2026-02-04 range of $175-185bn (Q4 2025 release) is entered as an earlier guidance row.

dc MGMT 2026-07-22: supply-constrained 'for multiple quarters in a row'; demand outpaces capacity. Q3 2026 plan: expand third-party capacity as a bridging strategy, which 'will create modest margin pressure in the near term' for Cloud; Wiz integration creates near-term headwinds; free cash flow 'will remain under pressure'; depreciation and data center operating costs (energy) keep rising; continued hiring in AI and Cloud; marketing for AI products.

dc MGMT 2026-07-22: Q3 FX is 'a slight headwind' to consolidated revenue (Q2 had a 1 point tailwind), mainly Search and YouTube ads; Search laps the acceleration that began in Q3 2025 (a tougher comparison). No numeric revenue, margin or tax guidance is given by the company in the release or call.

dc MGMT 2026-07-22: TPU system sales were delivered to customer data centers for the first time in Q2 2026 (revenue recognized in Google Cloud; inventory rose from $2.4bn at 2025-12-31 to $10.0bn). 'A relatively small portion' of revenue from existing TPU system agreements is recognized in 2026, ramping as 2026 ends; 'the vast majority' in 2027. These agreements are in the $514bn Cloud backlog ('multiple gigawatts', Q1 10-Q). Margin by product is not disclosed. Cloud revenue growth 'accelerated meaningfully even after excluding TPU system sales' (no number given).

dc MGMT 2026-07-22: capital structure. Sources of funding in order: cash from operations, then debt (about $16bn a year ago to about $100bn now), then equity 'to ensure a resilient balance sheet'. 'At this point, we're not planning to go back to the equity markets' except the ATM ($40bn, none sold at 2026-06-30) used for tax obligations on stock-based awards 'for some period of time'. Waymo: no change of structure planned ('Alphabet continues to provide long-term support and capital').

dc MGMT 2026-07-22 (Pichai): the company says it is the Gemini coding gap that needs improvement; Gemini 4 pretraining has started ('most ambitious yet'), a 'much larger base model'; Gemini 3.5 Pro in testing. Compute allocation order: frontier model development first, then serving Search/YouTube and Cloud (Vertex, Gemini Enterprise). Input-cost inflation is reflected in pricing 'to see returns'. These are management statements, not facts.

dc DEFINITION: free cash flow in the release = operating cash flow minus purchases of property and equipment (Q2 2026: 39,069 - 44,924 = -5,855; TTM 53,273). It excludes finance leases, the $85.2bn of signed leases not yet commenced, and the $22bn purchased non-marketable securities in H1 2026. Capex is purchases of property and equipment only.

dc CASH: 'cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities' of $242.5bn includes $87.1bn of marketable equity securities, of which $80.0bn is SpaceX shares under short-term sale restrictions (another $14.1bn of SpaceX shares sits in other non-current assets, restricted through Q3 2027). Equity-security gains are mark-to-market and not spendable liquidity until sold; cash and cash equivalents alone are $55.9bn and debt securities about $100.5bn.

dc ONE-OFFS Q2 2026: (1) gain on equity securities $99.0bn pre-tax, 'primarily unrealized gains from SpaceX and a private company' (company: raised the tax provision by $21.9bn, net income by $77.1bn, EPS by $6.26); it is non-operating and mark-to-market, not repeatable at this size (Q1 2026: $36.9bn of equity gains in OI&E, Q2 2025: $1.3bn). (2) PriceRunner (Klarna) damages $2.1bn accrued in Q2: $1.5bn in G&A (Google Services) and $581m interest and costs in OI&E; appealed. (3) EC Android fine and interest $5.2bn was already accrued and was paid in July 2026 (a Q3 cash outflow, no Q3 expense). The Q2 effective tax rate of 19.1% is distorted by deferred tax on unrealized gains.

dc DEFINITION CHANGES: from Q1 2026 revenue backlog (RPO) includes contracts with an original term of one year or less (so Q1 2026 vs Q4 2025 is not like-for-like: $467.6bn vs $242.8bn); Q2 2026 vs Q1 2026 is on the same basis (+$51.9bn total, +$51.6bn Cloud). Cloud revenue includes TPU system sales from Q2 2026 (product revenue) and Wiz from 2026-03-11. Wiz and Intersect (closed 2026-03-10) add acquired revenue and cost to 2026 comparisons; the acquired revenue is not disclosed separately in the documents read.

dc SHARES: shares outstanding rose from 12,088m (2025-12-31) to 12,230m (2026-06-30) after the June 2026 raise (29m Class A at $355.1982 + 29m Class C at $351.8018 public; 14m A + 14m C to an affiliate of Berkshire Hathaway, $10.0bn; net proceeds $30.5bn) and 19m shares of 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred (net $19.1bn, $1,000 liquidation preference, dividends $12.15 a share per quarter on each series, converts about 2029-05-15 into 2.2520-2.8160 Class A (Series A) or 2.2740-2.8420 Class C (Series B) per preferred share, i.e. about 21-27m Class A shares and 22-27m Class C shares (9.5m preferred shares per series), 43-54m in total, subject to adjustments; capped calls with a $1.0bn premium and caps of $532.67 (A) and $527.80 (C)). The diluted count already includes 16m if-converted preferred shares (Q2). No buybacks in H1 2026 ($69.5bn authorization left; $45.7bn repurchased in FY2025). Dividend $0.22 a share a quarter. SBC $7.96bn in Q2 2026.

dc DEBT: long-term debt face $101.1bn at 2026-06-30 (vs $49.1bn at 2025-12-31); 2026 issues: $20.0bn USD notes (weighted coupon 4.80%, 15 years), GBP 5.5bn (5.31%, 31 years), CHF 3.1bn, EUR 9.0bn (3.90%, 13 years), CAD 8.5bn (4.35%, 15 years), JPY 576.5bn (2.65%, 8 years). Interest expense rose from $261m (Q2 2025) to $1,278m (Q2 2026). Credit facilities $11.7bn ($1.3bn drawn), commercial paper program $25bn (none outstanding). Fair value of notes $94.9bn.

dc COMMITMENTS: purchase commitments and other contractual obligations $811.0bn at 2026-06-30 ($200.7bn short-term) vs $149.1bn at 2025-12-31 ($113.0bn short-term). Note 10: fixed or guaranteed commitments over one year $707.0bn, 'significant majority' long-term supply agreements for technical infrastructure and inventory components, mostly fulfilled through 2030; energy take-or-pay agreements 2 to 26 years (to 2054) with substantive termination fees. Beyond these: $85.2bn of data-center leases signed but not commenced (2026-2031), a $5.8bn short-term lease starting Q3 2026, backstops $7.6bn (guarantees) and $43.8bn (credit derivatives) plus $24.1bn more agreed subject to terms, and $20.0bn of milestone-contingent funding to a private company (equity derivative; was $10.0bn commitment plus $30.0bn contingent at 2026-03-31).

dc BACKLOG: revenue backlog $519.5bn at 2026-06-30, $513.9bn Google Cloud; 'just over 50%' to be recognized in the next 24 months (so about $260bn+ in 24 months, remainder later); it excludes cancellable contracts. Management: 'majority of the backlog is typical GCP contracts for a broad mix of customers'; TPU system sales are inside it; the split of AI-lab contracts vs other customers, and customer names and concentration inside the backlog, are not disclosed (gap).

dc CUSTOMERS: the 10-K states that no individual customer or group of affiliated customers represented more than 10% of revenues in 2023, 2024 or 2025 (10-K revenue note, saved text reading/10k_full.txt line 1625). No customer shares are therefore entered. Cloud backlog customer concentration is not disclosed; the call names examples (PepsiCo, Intel, HSBC, Bell Canada, Macy's, Signal Iduna, Booking Holdings, Morgan Stanley, Pfizer, Roche, Kakao, Deutsche Boerse, Blackstone for TPU data-center projects) without sizes.

dc RISK 1: advertising dependence: more than 70% of 2025 revenues from online advertising; advertisers and distribution partners can cancel; AI is reshaping ad formats (10-K Item 1A, first risk factor).

dc RISK 2: capital intensity and capacity: Alphabet expects to 'significantly expand' investment in technical infrastructure; depreciation and useful-life changes pressure operating margin; ability to scale is constrained by power, water and land; supply shortages, price increases and long-term commitments ($811bn, 10-Q Item 2) can leave unconsumed materials (10-K Item 1A 'manufacturing and supply chain risks'; 10-Q liquidity section).

dc RISK 3: antitrust and regulatory: US Search final judgment (December 2025; appeals by both sides, data-sharing and syndication remedies), US ad tech remedies decision pending with possible structural remedies (DOJ), EC adtech fine EUR 3.0bn (appealed), EC DMA findings, Epic/Play remedies, EC Android fine now final ($5.2bn paid July 2026), PriceRunner $2.1bn; $17.4bn of short-term legal and regulatory accruals (10-Q Note 10; 10-K Item 1A 'laws, regulations').

dc RISK 4: competition in AI and search: intense competition from large companies and start-ups; frontier model quality, coding gap acknowledged by management, risk that AI answers displace search queries or ad clicks (10-K Item 1A 'We face intense competition'; transcript Q&A).

dc RISK 5: revenue growth rate could decline and operating margin face downward pressure from higher investment in technical infrastructure, depreciation, TAC and new businesses (10-K Item 1A 'Our revenue growth rate could decline over time').

dc RISK 6: financing and balance sheet: access to debt and equity markets, leases and interest cost; debt up from about $16bn to about $100bn in a year, interest expense about 5 times higher y/y, equity and mandatory convertible issued June 2026, FCF negative in Q2 2026 (10-K Item 1A on capital markets; 10-Q Notes 6 and 11; call).

dc RISK 7: fair-value volatility of investments: the Q2 2026 net income includes $99.0bn of mainly unrealized equity gains (SpaceX, a private company); non-marketable carrying value rests on observable transactions and valuation models, and OI&E can swing sharply either way (10-K Item 1A 'fluctuations in the fair values of our investments'; 10-Q Note 3).

dc RISK 8: ownership and control: Class B shares carry 10 votes; Larry Page and Sergey Brin beneficially owned approximately 89.3% of 'our' [the rest of the sentence is cut by a page break in the saved 10-K text; read it as their share of the Class B stock/voting power, unverified] as of 2025-12-31 (Item 1A, 'concentration of our stock ownership'); Class C has no votes. Also: international revenue about 52% of 2025 consolidated revenue (FX, trade, tax); energy and supply-chain geopolitics.

dc GAP: not found or not disclosed in the documents read: (a) numeric company guidance for revenue, margin, tax rate or share count (none given; only capex range and qualitative statements); (b) Q2 2026 paid-subscription count (last disclosed 350m at Q1 2026); (c) YouTube subscriptions and Cloud revenue split between core GCP, AI infrastructure, Workspace and TPU sales; (d) backlog by customer or by contract type; (e) FY2025 revenue-line detail (Search, YouTube, Network, subscriptions) for the full year was not read, only the quarters; (f) the Q1 2026 call transcript (only the Q2 call was fetched, one AV call).

dc CHECK: the companyfacts first-filed value for repurchases in Q2 2025 (13,638m, prefetch quarter_case) differs from the cash flow statement line 'Repurchases of stock' (13,238m, release and 10-Q); the quarter case uses 13,238m. All other prefetch quarter lines (revenue, operating income, net income, operating cash flow, capex, SBC) reconcile to the release.

dc QUARTER REVIEW (understand/quarter_result.json, case understand/quarter_case.json): Q2 2026 revenue +24.2% y/y, operating income +30.4%, operating margin 34.0% (Q1 2026 36.1%, Q2 2025 32.4%). Reported net income $112.2bn (EPS $9.11) normalizes to $36.8bn (about $2.99 on 12,309m diluted shares) after removing the $77.1bn after-tax equity gain and adding back the PriceRunner charge ($1.2bn G&A and $0.47bn OI&E after tax at the reported 19.1% rate, deductibility unknown). Opex +26.7% reported, +20.9% ex the $1.5bn legal charge, below revenue growth; incremental operating margin 40.6%. Liquidity: spendable $162.5bn (cash 55.9 + marketable debt and unrestricted equity 106.6), $80.0bn of restricted SpaceX shares kept apart, debt $100.2bn, net cash $62.3bn. Guidance row: FY2026 capex midpoint $200bn, raised 8.1% vs the prior $185bn midpoint, 119% above FY2025 capex of $91.4bn. Engine flags: headline_distorted (high), peak_margin_run_rate (high; the history lines are annual margins, median 30.6%, max 32.1%, while Q1 2026 was already 36.1%, so Q2 34.0% is not a one-quarter spike), weak_cash_conversion (Q2 FCF -$5.9bn), profit_concentration (Google Services 82% of segment profit), Other Bets margin compression. No consensus data was supplied (gather_numbers owns it), so there is no vs-expectations read.

dc ECON REVIEW (understand/econ_result.json, case understand/econ_case.json): the engine rule alone, given Cloud/software words in the profile, picked data_platform_software as primary and ads_platform as secondary; that was replaced by a written analyst override (ads_platform primary, data_platform_software secondary, evidence: 10-K advertising more than 70% of 2025 revenue, 10-Q, Q2 release). Computed: SBC 6.6% of revenue and backlog (RPO) 4.3 times quarterly revenue (Cloud backlog 20.7 times Cloud's quarterly revenue). Open (not disclosed by Alphabet): daily active users and ARPU for Search/YouTube, Cloud customer counts and revenue per customer, net revenue retention. Flag segment_unexplained (high): Google Services is 79% of revenue and 85% of segment profit with no model KPIs disclosed. Gemini App MAU (950m) and AI Mode MAU (over 1bn) are not ads-platform dau/mau and were deliberately not entered as such.
gaps: No numeric guidance for revenue, margins, tax rate or share count exists in the release or call; only the FY2026 capex range ($195-205bn, raised from $180-190bn) and qualitative Q3 and 2027 statements.

The $180-190bn capex range (between the Feb 2026 $175-185bn and the Jul 2026 $195-205bn) is known only as 'previous estimate' in the Q2 call: its issue date and source (Q1 call, 2026-04-29, presumably) were not fetched.
Q3 2026 results (expected on or about 2026-10-28 per an unverified third-party calendar) are after the as_of and are not in the evidence; the analyst treats Q2 2026 as the latest reported quarter.
Customer shares: none above 10% (10-K); Cloud backlog concentration and customer names are not disclosed; no customer rows entered.
Paid subscriptions after Q1 2026 (350m) and a core-GCP versus TPU versus AI-infrastructure split of Cloud revenue are not disclosed.
Only one transcript (Q2 2026) was fetched; the Q1 2026 call and its capex statement were not read.
stopped: Stopped reading further documents once segments, backlog, commitments, capital raise, guidance, risks and the call were covered; the tool-call budget (about 22) was exceeded by a few calls while reading the 10-Q notes and quarter.py/econ.py formats, with no refetch of prefetch material.
A WebSearch for the Q3 2026 results date returned no company confirmation; not pursued further.
